headline: Generative and causal models target biomedical counterfactuals where intervention is costly
label: Generative Models For Biomedical Counterfactuals
summary: Observational and single-cell datasets demand counterfactual estimates that handle confounding and separate technical from biological variation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned causal and generative modeling for counterfactual questions where direct intervention is costly or unavailable. SCOUT estimates ATE and CATE in observational biomedical data via two-dimensional confounder adjustment, and LaMe estimates natural direct and indirect effects in a joint linear-Gaussian latent mediation framework for high-dimensional systems. On the single-cell side, scDeepSim couples a structured VAE with a latent diffusion simulator to enable controlled intervention on biological and technical factors for benchmarking, while scCody uses generative optimal transport to model age-dependent population dynamics and separate aging-aligned from divergent disease-associated remodeling. Related work benchmarks temporal causal discovery on simulated kinetic networks with latent confounders, and PhysInfer infers transcriptional burst parameters from static scRNA-seq. What is new is the use of explicit generative simulators and latent-variable structure to make counterfactual variation controllable and testable.
